matchups.analysis: Rinor's walking out with this one at 100%—119.1 final, done scoring, and Rob's stuck at 111.3 with absolutely nothing left to play and an 8-point hole that's genuinely his own doing. Rob benched Michael Wilson (20.4) to start Jadarian Price (0.7), which is a 19.7-point swing that would've made this competitive instead of a forgone conclusion—that's not projection variance, that's just watching your best available option sit on the bench while you start a guy who contributed literally nothing. De'Von Achane dropping 1.7 on a 17.3 projection didn't help Rinor either, but his Vikings D/ST going nuclear for 19.0 on a 6.5 projection actually bailed him out anyway, which tells you everything about having depth that Rinor's roster execution was already good enough without needing the defense to carry him. Rob's got nobody left to blame and no runway left to fix it—this one's locked down because one catastrophically bad bench decision turned what could've been close into a blowout.

Adam's walking out with 3% and nothing left to play, which is the polite way of saying this thing's been over since halftime—ESPN's got him at 74.8 final while Flamur cruises home with 97.7 projected and Saquon plus Wicks still warming up on the bench. George Kittle dragged Adam kicking and screaming with a 12.7-point overperformance, but then Justin Jefferson decided to tank by 10.6 points, and that self-inflicted wound of benching Pat Bryant (13.4) for Xavier Worthy (3.0)—a full 10.4-point swing—basically murdered any shot at competitive football before the second half even started. Flamur didn't need his starters to do anything crazy; Tee Higgins just casually beat her projection by 7.6 points and that was enough cushion to coast, which is what happens when you're betting on depth executing while your opponent's already sabotaged his own lineup and run out of time to recover.

Rilind's getting absolutely demolished here—ESPN's projecting a 59-point final gap (73.8 to 132.9) with only 1% win probability, and this thing is completely done before DeVonta Smith even takes the field. You benched Harold Fannin Jr. for 20.6 points to roll out Oronde Gadsden, who showed up and scored a grand total of zero while projecting for nearly 7, which is the kind of self-inflicted 20.6-point swing that doesn't just lose games—it gets remembered for years. Arben's got Jaxon Smith-Njigba absolutely torching his projection (30.4 on 17.2) and Jonathan Taylor underperforming (8.2 on 19.1) and he's still up 59 because his entire roster is just executing while yours is actively sabotaging itself. Even Bhayshul Tuten's 5.8-point overperformance can't rescue this when your lineup decision just handed away two full touchdowns before halftime.

Jetmir and Peter are walking out with 1% odds and a 74-point projected deficit that's already dead before Luther Burden even takes the field—Nori didn't need Jahmyr Gibbs to go absolutely nuclear for 37.9 on a 23.4 projection, he just needed his entire roster to be objectively better constructed than yours, and that's exactly what happened. You benched Keaton Mitchell for 12.2 points to start Rhamondre Stevenson for 5.3, which would be a punch-yourself-in-the-face move on any normal week, but it's genuinely irrelevant when you're already getting demolished by 74 points and Tetairoa McMillan is collapsing from 11.9 projected to a pathetic 2.7 actual. Kenneth Walker keeping you within shouting distance at 20.3 doesn't matter when your depth is pulling you under and Nori's entire secondary crew is just executing safer, more reliable performances across the board—this one's locked and you've got nothing left but the knowledge that you actively self-sabotaged yourself on the bench for no reason whatsoever.

Ilir's walking out with this locked at 100% while Ben's staring at 0% with all his guys done and nothing left but regret—that 8.8-point deficit is entirely self-inflicted because he benched Juwan Johnson (19.3 actual) to start Dalton Kincaid (2.8 actual), a 16.5-point swing that would've made this competitive if he'd spent thirty seconds thinking about tight end matchups instead of just guessing. Bijan Robinson turned his 17.3 projection into 34.3 and basically carried the entire load while Ben watched KC Concepcion (1.9 on 9.2) completely disappear and his own bench piece outscore his starting tight end by seven times over—that's the kind of week where you can't blame variance, only your own decisions staring you right in the face before Sunday even started.

Faton's walking out with this at 99% and a projected 21.2-point cushion that basically makes Swift and Loveland ceremonial at this point—ESPN's got the math done and Veton's sitting at 1% with nothing left to play and a 21.2-point hole that screams "this was over when you benched Wan'Dale Robinson." You left 10.5 points on the board by starting Bateman over Robinson on a night you needed every single one, and somehow that's not even the worst part: you benched Chris Bell (8.7 actual) to start Shaheed (2.4 actual), which cost you another 6.3 points when your entire game plan was "hope Brock Purdy carries me"—well, he did his job with 31.3 on a 20.8 projection, but you decided to sabotage the rest of the roster anyway and now you're watching your season die because of two consecutive lineup decisions that ranged from mediocre to actively stupid. Drake London already beat his projection by 11 points for Faton while you're stuck at your final total wondering why you keep outsmarting yourself at the wrong times.
